title: Meditation, David Darling and Music for People
summary: Asked about jazz education, he describes meditation begun with Ellington and workshops with David Darling.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: On the way up we were talking a little bit about jazz education, and all the students that are doing it nowadays.
Well I’ve really gotten into that a lot.

I’ve never worked to get the work but I’m getting ready to do that now. You know I’ve got some management people I’m starting to work with. But I told you I had started meditating when I started working with Duke. And that was a whole kind of path, I didn’t even know it was connected with music. Then I ended up taking all kinds of workshops and visualization, manifestation, yoga, Tai Chi. You know David Darling by any chance?

He had a great thing that I used to sit in. I took some classes with him called “Music for People,” about just teaching groups of people from a concert violinist to someone who never did music in their lives, to making good music together. And it was brilliant. And he invited me to come to this thing he did, it was in ’86, like a week-long thing in the summer where I would just hang out and be part of it. And so I grew, both fields started coming together, seeing how you could help teach someone. And the first time I really realized this was a guy’s coming into my house for lessons. And I’ve been contemplating this. I sat next to Cootie Williams for three years. And he was a good friend. And how he played [scats] laid back so far, and it just told so much and just sound, not a lot of notes, but the sound. So I thought about this. How do you give someone the experience of playing with Cootie Williams, which you can’t even buy now. This kid walks in the door
